notes.v120_design_change: The central change in V1.2.0 is not renaming fields, it is a change of paradigm. V1.1.0 asserted field existence, which required keys that do not exist. V1.2.0 measures dependence by contrast: run paired scenarios A (full coverage, no conflicts) and B (no coverage), and require the downstream conclusion to differ. Consumption is a dependency relation and a dependency can only be proven by changing the input and observing the output. Contrast also cannot be satisfied vacuously, which mechanically removes the vacuous-PASS problem that V1.1.0 had in S2, since a downstream that always returns an empty array now yields A equal to B and fails.

Delivered all seven requests: R1 coverageStatus on downstream output, R1b upstreamStatus on downstream input, R2 kycGaps[].status, R3 executionStatus on upstream output, R4 conflicts[].id, R5 ban on placeholder ruleIds, R6 taskId and asOf. Also added assertions to validate_bank_front_skills.py so the new fields are checked automatically. My key audit now verifies 55 declared keys all present in the four real contract files with zero warnings, up from 46.
notes.my_request_was_incomplete: R1 as originally written only asked for a downstream OUTPUT field, which would not have worked. The downstream had no INPUT field through which to learn upstream state, so the structural path could not have been driven. I added R1b during implementation. The lesson: before requesting a field, ask where its value comes from. A contract is a chain, not a set of points.
notes.review_found_design_flaw: The independent reviewer found that V1.2.0 S2(b) and S3(b) compared downstream(A) with downstream(B) as evidence of consumption, but the downstream is an LLM and identical input twice already produces different output, which I had measured myself in the previous cycle. So the difference proves nothing and S3(b) passes by chance about half the time. V1.2.1 adds a within-scenario stability precondition: k of at least three runs per scenario must agree before cross-scenario difference counts, and instability yields INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS. Divergence must now be structural rather than a length comparison.
notes.headline_lesson_this_round: A falsified assumption must be registered as forbidden, not merely noted as a failure. I recorded that S5 failed, but treated it as an observation instead of upgrading it into the constraint that a non-deterministic downstream forbids cross-scenario difference as evidence. So I used it in the very next design. Recording is not constraining.
notes.v121_not_preregistered: V1.2.1 is NOT preregistered and must not be. The review fixes are themselves new design that has never been executed. Per owner ruling 1 it needs a second independent review before locking. Two of the eight fixes are structural changes to judging method, not wording, so assuming they are correct would repeat the V1.2.0 mistake.
notes.second_review: Second independent review, run from the prompt I authored, found three verified problems. The worst is a circularity: section 2.1 wrote scenario B missing-indicator names into the downstream input field kycMissingFields, while S3(b) required the output to reference those same names, so the harness supplied the answer and then checked for it. A downstream that merely echoes that input field passes. I had fixed the output side when the flaw was on the construction side. Also verified: my claim that section 4 is audit-covered was false, since the citations sit in bullet lines the parser did not read; and the R1-R6 delivery left the document self-contradictory because I updated the new facts but not the old statements they invalidated.
notes.headline_lesson_second_review: A measurement setup must not supply the answer it then checks for. Any design where the harness writes the expected result into the input is circular regardless of how strict the output check is, and the fix must be on the construction side, not the output side.
notes.review_history: Three rounds now, none of them found by me: round 1 judged that 3 of 5 criteria keys did not exist in the contracts; round 2 reviewed and found the contrast criteria were fooled by LLM non-determinism; round 3 reviewed and found the circularity plus two fixes that did not actually work. Each round also found defects introduced by the previous round fixes.
notes.second_review_critical_finding: The most serious defect of three rounds: my criteria punished compliant downstreams and rewarded contract violation. S2(b)/S3(b) required kycGaps to differ between scenarios, but both scenarios are trigger-less and the contract requires a compliant downstream to return an empty gap list in both, distinguishing them only via coverageStatus. So compliant fails and a downstream that fabricates a gap, which the contract forbids, passes. Root cause: I introduced it with my own R1 delivery. Providing the correct channel made compliant downstreams stop changing kycGaps while my criteria still inspected kycGaps. Changing a contract changes the behaviour of the thing being measured, and I never re-derived the criteria.
notes.v122_changes: V1.2.2 deletes the cross-scenario kycGaps comparison from S2 and S3. S3 keeps only the structured coverageStatus path. S2 returns to pure negative with an explicit note that its power comes from pairing with S3. stable() is narrowed to S5. The document now states S3 proves transfer-level consumption only, not understanding. Also fixed: audit not covering section 4, 37 of 55 wrong source line numbers, stale pending-KERT markers, and a title that contradicted its own status section.
notes.new_line_audit: scripts/gk_ke_criteria_line_audit.py checks that every cited file:line actually points at the field. It found 37 of 55 wrong and can rewrite them, so line numbers are now generated and verified by machine rather than hand-typed. The old audit captured line numbers but never used them.
notes.owner_ruling_role_change: Owner agreed to change the working method: TL no longer authors criteria. TL provides the problem statement, contract facts, measured evidence and mechanical audit tooling; an independent party authors the criteria. I handed over a role document plus a nine-item list of design patterns that three rounds empirically falsified, registered as forbidden rather than merely as failed.
notes.why_i_stepped_down: Three rounds ran and none of the defects was found by me; rounds 2 and 3 both found defects introduced by the previous round fixes. Structural reason: I was simultaneously the criteria author and the driver of contract evolution, so every fix of mine changed the thing being measured and invalidated my own assumptions about downstream behaviour. No amount of self-care removes an author blind spot that three independent rounds have measured.
notes.tl_retained_permissions: TL retains: problem statement and acceptance criteria, contract facts, mechanical audit tooling, running audits and reporting results, recording failures as negative material. TL must not author, edit or modify criteria content, must not relax audits for a particular criterion, and must not evaluate whether the author output is acceptable.
